title: The text discusses the life and tragic murder of Ali Mecili, a prominent Algerian lawyer and human rights activist, who was shot by a man with a black umbrella in Paris. Known for his unwavering commitment to justice, Mecili had been living under threat from the Algerian government due to his involvement in human rights campaigns and his efforts to reconcile historical leaders of the Algerian revolution. His death raises concerns about the return of violent political methods in Algeria, reminiscent of past conflicts that resulted in significant casualties among Algerians. The text also reflects on the historical context of political violence in Algeria, highlighting the ongoing vendetta culture and the impact of past civil wars on current political dynamics.
